service_indicators_found: sc-agent-http UreqTransport: blocking HTTP client with busy retry, timeouts, response caps (crates/sc-agent-http/src/retry.rs, ureq_transport.rs)

findings.issue: Expired session documents are never deleted. Each live run that selects an ask-capable backend writes one <id>.json (up to about 96 KB) into the sessions directory. Expiry (is_expired, lines 244-248; read_session, lines 238-240) only refuses to load the file. The only cleanup, sweep_stale_tmp (lines 508-528, called from FileSessionStore::new at line 137), removes *.tmp.* files, so the directory grows without bound. Session versions 1 and 2 are also refused on read but are never removed.
findings.recommendation: Extend the sweep in FileSessionStore::new to remove <id>.json files whose created_at (or mtime) is older than the TTL, using the same cutoff logic as is_expired. Alternatively, document the retention policy and provide an explicit prune command. The sweep already runs once per live run, so the added cost is one metadata read per json file.
findings.evidence: sweep_stale_tmp filters on name.contains(TMP_MARKER) and returns before touching any non-tmp file (lines 516-518). The doc comment at lines 42-47 states the sweep covers temporary files only. A grep of crates/sc-jev-check/src for remove_file shows only tmp-file removals (lines 470, 525).

findings.issue: The session-log flush is skipped on the error path. HostRun::run calls run(self.prepared)? (line 344), so when every backend fails and run returns Err, the flush warning is never produced. The adapter is then dropped, and LoggerInner::drop discards flush and shutdown errors (crates/sc-jev-host/src/obs.rs:45-52). A flush failure on the path where failed send rows matter most is therefore silent. ask_from has the same shape: ask(...)? at compose.rs:419 returns before finish_log at line 420.
findings.recommendation: Flush before propagating the error, for example by splitting run into a match that always calls finish_log and then returns the error. When the run fails, surface the flush failure through the error's detail or the stderr channel, so the loss is observable. Keep the drop-time flush as the last resort.
findings.evidence: compose.rs:343-349 (HostRun::run) and compose.rs:418-423 (ask_from). Warning only on the success path: finish_log is reached only after the ? operator has succeeded. obs.rs:45-52 uses let _ = for both flush and shutdown in Drop.

findings.issue: The sc-observability envelope leaves request_id and correlation_id as None, while the row carries session_id and answer_id as ULIDs in fields{} only. Generic log tooling that correlates on envelope fields cannot join rows to a session or to a send.
findings.recommendation: Populate the envelope correlation field with the session id (and request_id with the answer id, if the envelope type accepts ULIDs). Keep fields{} unchanged, so the row contract does not change.
findings.evidence: ObservabilityAdapter::log_event sets request_id: None (line 196) and correlation_id: None (line 197) for every event, while event.fields() carries session_id and answer_id.

findings.issue: Every session-log event is emitted at Level::Info, whether the send succeeded or failed. A failed send (send_outcome = "failed", with error_code set) is indistinguishable by level from a successful one, so level-based filtering or alerting at WARN or ERROR cannot see failed sends.
findings.recommendation: Derive the level from the row's send_outcome: Level::Warn for failed sends and Level::Info for ok sends. Level::Warn and Level::Error both exist in sc-observability 1.5.0.
findings.evidence: log_event hard-codes level: Level::Info (line 188). The event's fields carry send_outcome, which SessionLogRow::to_fields sets to "failed" for failed sends (crates/sc-decision-schema/src/session_log/mod.rs:244-247).
